description: Table 1 of the paper, rendered as a single two-row table with no additional panels or insets. The header row lists seven element symbols from left to right: Fe, Mn, Al, Si, C, P, S, separated by a horizontal rule from the data row beneath. The data row reads, in the same order: Bal., 7.79, 4.88, 0.84, 0.2, 0.03, 0.03. No units are printed inside the table image itself; the caption states that the values are chemical composition in wt.%. No other rows, columns, footnotes, colour coding or graphical elements are present — the image contains only these two text rows. The table therefore reports the measured bulk chemistry of the Al-added medium Mn steel studied in the paper, with Fe given as the balance and the alloying additions Mn, Al and Si plus the interstitial C and the residual impurities P and S. The citing text states the composition was measured by XRF (X-ray fluorescence) and OES (optical emission spectroscopy) and identifies the designed grade as Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) low-density medium Mn steel, consistent with the tabulated values. The table is a compositional input to the downstream thermomechanical processing (homogenisation, forging, rolling and intercritical annealing at 750 °C) rather than a results panel.

observations.observation: The table has a single data row beneath a header row listing the elements Fe, Mn, Al, Si, C, P, S in that order.
Iron is reported as 'Bal.' (balance) rather than as a numeric value.
Aluminium content is printed as 4.88 and silicon content as 0.84.
Carbon content is printed as 0.2, and both phosphorus and sulphur are printed as 0.03.
No unit is printed inside the table image; all values are printed without a % symbol or wt.% label.
The caption states the tabulated values are the chemical composition in wt.% of an Al-added medium Mn steel.
The citing text states the final chemical composition of the developed steel was measured using XRF (X-ray fluorescence) and OES (optical emission spectroscopy).
The citing text identifies the designed grade as low-density Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) medium Mn steel, which is consistent with the tabulated Mn, Al and C values.

The citing text states the steel was made by a melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace (Power Trak 250-10 R Inductotherm), then homogenised at 1100 °C for 2 h and hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the range 1050-800 °C.
The citing text states intercritical annealing was performed at 750 °C (IA750) for 5, 30, 60, 120 and 180 minutes followed by air cooling.
